starting_principles: Chain rule formulation of acceleration a = v dv/dx

ordered_steps.action_description: Apply chain rule to express acceleration without explicit time dependence
ordered_steps.justification: Chain rule of calculus where v = dx/dt.
Separation of variables for first-order differential form.

ordered_steps.action_description: Integrate from initial state (x = 0, v = u) to final state (x = s, v = v)

ordered_steps.equation_latex: \left[ \frac{v^2}{2} \right]_{u}^{v} = a [x]_{0}^{s} \implies \frac{v^2 - u^2}{2} = a s \implies v^2 = u^2 + 2 a s
ordered_steps.justification: Integration of linear function v and constant a.

applicability_conditions: Valid for 1D rectilinear motion under constant acceleration
source_references: Fundamentals of Physics by Halliday, Resnick & Walker (Chapter 2, p. 32)
